title: Is this UI AI-y?
author: PupperRobot
selftext: Title. I actually designed the UI layout myself but I'm wondering if it still gives off ai vibes? To me it looks very nice and shows everything I want to show in a clear and concise way. One feedback ai driven UI always gets the website-y look so in my layout I tried to avoid that but frankly I'm not sure how else to design my UI.

comments.author: ConfusedBaka69
comments.body:
The hand looks a little too detailed
Besides that gives me like...age of empires vibes? Strong hold? Something like that

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Well those are the vibes I'm going for so I'll take it 😁

replies.author: ConfusedBaka69
replies.body: Good good, but yea I've noticed Claude tends to over detail and define hands, especially the parts of the fingers that bend, idk of your using claude tho but just my 2 cents.

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: It was actually astra that designed the icons via my prompts. I noticed astra compared to Sol for instance always adds a bit of extra realism even if the desired output is stylized.

replies.author: ConfusedBaka69
replies.body: Ah well Claude did the same and I had Astra fix it up for me but I tend to use gpt for image gen or switch if one is doing something I don't like or if I'm having a hard time explaining and having the ai actually change the style, or make it how I want it to look.

comments.author: Lord_Forwind
comments.body: Not really seems fairly normal. The big green blank space in the top right is the only ai feeling thing since normal devs try to avoid that empty space

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Good feedback! I'll try to utilize that space! Thank you

comments.author: ackley14
comments.body:
yes but only because AI has a tendancy to island things. like everything looks like it's on its own island, the wooden buttons on b0ottom are one island, the abilities and traits are a second island, the icons above are a bit of an island and probably the least AI looking part of this.

i think it's the mashing of a variety of looks in one single screen that screams AI the most. typically UI is consistent and features callbacks to other UI elements.

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: But I designed the layout myself. Admittedly I'm bad at UI design. How else do I not island things? To me that seems like a logical thing to do also. Am I a robot?

comments.author: Icy-Fudge5222
comments.body: I'd change the colors. Probably unfair, but like em dashes the yellow/brown color scheme is now considered Claude Coded.

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: But that wasn't even Claude coded 😭 those were human designed via my direction. Hate that we have to change things now because ai also does things that way.

replies.author: Icy-Fudge5222
replies.body: I understand that, I am just telling you how people will perceive it. People aren't allowed to use em dashes anymore either without being labled ai. Just how it is.

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: I see. Thanks. That sucks because my game takes place in the bronze age. And the color scheme of that entire era is basically various shades of yellow and brown with some rock elements.

replies.author: Ok-Pirate5732
replies.body: You can try to play more with blues and reds, the bronze age civilizations in the mediterranean and mesopotamia used a lot of striking blues both in their paintings and ceramic/tilework. Look at reconstructions of Minoan and Babylonian palaces, they are very vivid

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Makes sense! I'll try them out!

comments.author: golfstreamer
comments.body: I wouldn't call it "AI-y". It feels a bit plain and generic, though . But keep in mind I'm seeing it out of context of playing the actual game. (It might feel right during the flow of the game).

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Good feedback. My goal before launch is to have a human UI designed have a final look and point out obvious flaws. I wanted it to be a bit plain to be honest. Figured simplicty could be a good trait here but I'll ask my future UI guy.

comments.author: Ok-Pirate5732
comments.body:
a little bit, because claude loves to overdo the icon + title, especially with the hotkey as well. 

I'd start by at least putting the \[control+A\] in attack move as a hover tooltip, not in the button itself

Some other things I noticed that aren't necessarily AI tells: 

\- Spacing seems a little off. Some numbers are slightly below the icon, some are higher.   
\- Why does damage have no icon when everything else there is an icon?   
\- Not enough spacing below the line in Abilities and traits?   
\- Ready for Orders also seems oddly placed there as everything else is a statistic, could be easier to read elsewhere. 

  
Anyway, really cool that you made it yourself!

comments.author: gamedevjp
comments.body: Yes...it's the yellowish tint on everything imo

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Is there a way to prevent that?

replies.author: gamedevjp
replies.body: Tell your agent you want it to remove the tint. By default it uses that yellow on a lot of shit. I have this in my instructions for creating art because it's the #1 thing I see on all 2D AI art and I recognize it immediately

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: "Golden hour" lighting. Models use it a lot because it's a very popular lighting technique, thus permeated all throughout the training data.

replies.author: mrpoopistan
replies.body: Tell it what you want in terms of color palette and style. If you leave it to do what it wants, it will default to the AI style. Impose your aesthetics, which you should be doing anyhow.

replies.author: ConfusedBaka69
replies.body:
Personally I like it, maybe have a option to toggle or change the colors, also everyone finds AI in everything nowadays regardless if it's there or not so don't worry too much and don't fix a problem that's not there.


Tho a demo or actual thing to test would help judge more.

comments.author: Mitik85
comments.body: Tell it to change font … it always uses that font

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: I manually picked this font from Google fonts lol

replies.author: Mitik85
replies.body: Lol then you wouldn’t need to as it uses that or very close to that .. I mean your building a game UI not a powerpoint sheet that’s my two cent .. as far you get from  a pp sheet the best

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: Just change the font , and the green bar you’ll be fine

comments.author: Talongar
comments.body:
It's a bit flat and the the yellow tint kinda washed it out and makes it look more like a single image versus UI. 
I'd add small dropshadow to the icons, change the background tint to something more cool so that the buttons pop out more.

comments.author: oof-plap
comments.body: It's not too bad honestly, the only thing that really sticks out is the cluster of stats below the health bar. The AI looks like it wasn't sure how to prioritise or group the information so it just launched it all into a cluster.

comments.author: yojojomomo
comments.body: I think the top looks a bit hard to read, but the rest looks very human and I've seen similar ui in other games

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Why

replies.author: taisui
replies.body: It just looks like every other AI made UI

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Yeah in what way though? Because I designed the UI layout so I want to see what exactly AI does that makes it obviously similar

replies.author: taisui
replies.body: alignment, grids, fonts, the generic look of it.

comments.author: Wasdeq_Games
comments.body: Replace every . between text with a -

comments.author: InspectorInch
comments.body:
generate a UI of individual parts in chatgpt and then send them over to claude to assemble and animate

Have it generate 10-15 different ideas when generating the parts and pick which one looks the best

comments.author: hey_im_cool
comments.body: The reward hand looks weird like it was originally meant to be a right hand and the ai decided to turn the thumb into a pinky finger

comments.author: Winter_Aspect_8675
comments.body: Nothing about it really screams AI. I would focus on that stat block at the top and try square it up a bit and add a more consistent design language.
